title: Fncall replay delta notebook
content:
Context / goal:
Quick, messy notebook capturing a replay-based debugging approach for intermittent function-call + structured-output parsing failures we've been seeing in prod and staging. I want a reproducible minimal pipeline to (1) replay the exact sequence of tokens to the parser, (2) delta different parser configs (strict schema vs lenient fallback), and (3) capture exact byte-level mismatches so I can file a definitive bug report.

Summary of the failure mode observed:
- Symptom: downstream JSON parser occasionally throws `UnexpectedTokenError: expected \"\}\" but got \"\\n\"` even when the LLM output visually looks like valid JSON in logs.
- Frequency: ~1.7% of calls for the same prompt+model combo on dedicated pools during high throughput windows.
- Hypothesis: subtle streaming truncation or stray control characters; second hypothesis is the model injecting non-printing Unicode (ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE / U+FEFF) inside keys.

Repro playback plan (manual steps tried so far):
1) Grab raw response bytes from request id (example: req-0a7c3b) in S3. Saved to /tmp/replays/req-0a7c3b.bytes (binary).
2) Local quick check: run `xxd -b req-0a7c3b.bytes | sed -n '1,80p'` to scan for weird bytes. Found occasional 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF sequences (BOM) immediately before a `\"` char.

Commands & attempts (copied from terminal logs):
- curl-based replay (simulate the same streaming chunk boundaries):
  curl -v -X POST https://localhost:8080/replay -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @/tmp/replays/req-0a7c3b.bytes
  -> server returns 200 but parser fails with same stacktrace.

- Python requests with deterministic chunking (mimic the exact chunk sizes found in logs):
  CHUNKS = [512, 128, 1024, 256]  # experiment with different pacing and sizes
  with open('/tmp/replays/req-0a7c3b.bytes','rb') as f:
      for size in CHUNKS:
          chunk = f.read(size)
          requests.post('http://localhost:8080/chunk', data=chunk)
  -> parser fails when BOM bytes landed at chunk boundary.

Raw snippet showing offending bytes (hex / ascii):
00000020: 22 6b 65 79 22 3a 20 ef bb bf 22 76 61 6c 75 65 22 2c  "key": \xef\xbb\xbf"value",

Observation: BOM (EF BB BF) inserted between : and opening quote of value. JSON serializers normally tolerate BOM at start of document but not mid-document.

Stacktrace (prod tail - last 10 lines):
  at JSONParser._parseValue (json_parser.js:412:27)
  at JSONParser._parseObjectKey (json_parser.js:367:18)
  at JSONParser._parseObject (json_parser.js:298:14)
  at Function.parse (json_parser.js:52:10)
  at StructuredOutputHandler.parseThenValidate (structured_handler.ts:84:22)
  at Router.handleResponse (router.ts:217:11)
  => Top-level: UnexpectedTokenError: expected '}' but got '\n'

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): Model output contains invisible BOM sequences when the generator returns text that was originally produced with non-ASCII sources or certain tokenizers. The serving runtime's streaming logic concatenates chunks without normalizing/stripping internal BOM.
- H2: The streaming transport (internal websocket -> aggregator) re-encodes chunk boundaries with a multi-byte encoding that can split UTF-8 sequences across chunks; our reassembly code is not checking for incomplete UTF-8 sequences and assumes chunk boundaries align on character boundaries.
- H3: An upstream post-processing filter attempts to redact strings and inserts markers, which are then replaced with BOM-like bytes by accident. (lower priority)

What I tried to confirm H1/H2:
- run a small script that scans the last 10k tokens for non-printing codepoints: `python scan_unicode_garbage.py /tmp/replays/*.bytes` -> flagged U+FEFF and U+200B at ~450ish positions.
- reassemble bytes with explicit UTF-8 incremental decoder (Python):
  decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')()
  text = ''
  with open('req', 'rb') as f:
    while True:
      b = f.read(37)  # small to force boundary cases
      if not b: break
      text += decoder.decode(b)
  text += decoder.decode(b'', final=True)
  -> decoder raised UnicodeDecodeError when chunk split UTF-8 codepoint across reads. Means we need incremental decoding.

Delta experiments (what changed between runs):
- Parser config A: strict-json-parser (fail on any control char inside strings) -> reproducible fail 100% when BOM present.
- Parser config B: lenient parser (strip U+FEFF, U+200B before validation) -> downstream success, but that's hiding the root cause.

Minimal repro (to file for bug):
1) Create bytes: `printf '{\"key\": %s\"value\"}' "\xEF\xBB\xBF" > /tmp/min-bom.json`
2) Feed to parser: `node parse_min.js /tmp/min-bom.json` -> throws same UnexpectedTokenError.
3) Now feed same bytes but normalize: `cat /tmp/min-bom.json | tr -d '\\357\\273\\277' > /tmp/min-fixed.json` -> parses fine.

Questions / notes to file:
- Is BOM insertion coming from tokenizer -> sampling -> decode? We should check model tokenizer roundtrip for token ids that map to U+FEFF. Which model families have this behavior? (Observed on open-variant-v3 and a few community models.)
- Need to add UTF-8 incremental decoding guard in the streaming reassembly layer (serving runtime) so we never join incomplete multi-byte sequences naively.
- Add a lightweight sanitization step in StructuredOutputHandler to reject or explicitly strip control/invisible characters inside JSON strings when configured in strict mode, and emit events (parsing-warning) instead of silently stripping.

Next actions (todo):
- [ ] File JIRA-INF-8721 with minimal repro attached and link to req-0a7c3b bytes (I attached to the ticket draft).
- [ ] Add unit test to streaming-reassembly: simulate random chunk sizes and assert incremental UTF-8 decoding doesn't throw or produce replacement chars. Test in both Go and Node runtime components.
- [ ] Add diagnostic log flag to dedicated runtime to log chunk boundaries and presence of non-printing codepoints (opt-in, safe-to-enable).
- [ ] Reach out to model-onboarding team: do we strip BOMs during model conversion? (cc @Priya)

Notes from quick pairing with Evan (2024-10-30):
- Evan: we should instrument the reassembly to preserve byte offsets into the original response and emit a map of token index -> byte offset. That will make it possible to map token-level causes back to parser errors.
- Evan: Also try `jq --raw-output` on the byte stream to see if it surfaces the BOM differently.

Scratch/experiments appended below (raw):
- small Python snippet to detect internal BOMs: `b'\\xef\\xbb\\xbf' in open('file','rb').read()` -> quick but memory heavy.
- streaming check via node: `const dec = new TextDecoder('utf-8'); dec.decode(chunk, {stream:true})` vs {stream:false} behavior. I noticed Node's TextDecoder will replace malformed sequences with replacement glyph unless you use `fatal: true` option which then throws. That suggests adding `fatal` during debug runs to catch reassembly issues.

Open questions for later follow-up:
- Should we proactively sanitize model outputs from known invisible characters at the API boundary? Tradeoff: might mask model bugs and create divergence between raw model text and sanitized text.
- Are there legal/regulatory reasons to preserve exact bytes in logs? We need to keep an unmodified binary copy for forensic purposes. But also a sanitized copy for safe downstream parsing.

If anyone picks this up: start by replaying req-0a7c3b and run the `incremental-utf8-checker.py` (in my home dir). If you need a quick reproducer, use /tmp/min-bom.json sample above. Ping me (samira) or Evan in #dev-ex for pairing.

Changelog (this file):
- 2024-10-29: initial notes and first repro recorded
- 2024-10-30: added incremental-decoder experiment and Evan pairing notes
- 2024-11-02: confirmed BOM sequence present and created minimal repro file

-- end of notebook --
